video_title: Is LeBron Circumventing the Salary Cap With His New Sponsorship Deal?

quotes.speaker: Dan Le Batard
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James's massive off-court earnings and potential salary cap circumvention
quotes.excerpt: LeBron makes how much beyond his salary just sort of on the side in his career now?

text_blocks.speaker: Dan Le Batard
text_blocks.text: When you see LeBron James now, one of the biggest stories of the day is, wait a minute, LeBron makes how much beyond his salary just sort of on the side in his career now because they've opened up the gambling oil wells? And of course, if Kawhi Leonard and Uncle Dennis think they're worth that from Ballmer, what do you think LeBron thinks he's worth on the side when every city he goes to he improves the city's economy?

text_blocks.speaker: Amin Elhassan
text_blocks.text: I think there's a difference because LeBron, and if you don't know, the front office sports came out with a story, Ryan Glasspiegel wrote about this, about PolyMarket, which is a prediction market app, is paying LeBron 15 million dollars a year. There's a big ad that just came out. It's got him, it's got Eli Manning, it's got John Leguizamo, it's got Alexander Daddario, who I love very much. You've got all these people in there and it's announcing basically the LeBron arrival to PolyMarket and he's making 15 million a year off of this.

quotes.speaker: Amin Elhassan
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James's decision to take less money to join a team
quotes.excerpt: LeBron could have signed for a gazillion dollars in LA or the minimum in Philly or here.
quotes.quote: LeBron could have signed for a gazillion dollars in LA or the minimum in Philly or here or Cleveland. That deal was always going to be available for him. There's no way a brand would say, I don't know, LeBron for 15 million, I'm not sure. That's number one. And number two, he starred in an ad. Every time anyone says anything about any player getting paid on the side by a company or brand, oh, what about that one? You can't say that because Kawhi Leonard is not the level name star as LeBron, but he didn't do anything and that was the end-all be-all.

quotes.speaker: Dan Le Batard
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Ballmer's influence on college sports and potential salary cap issues
quotes.excerpt: I did not know before you guys did the reporting that Steve Ballmer could be such a booster.
quotes.quote: I did not know before you guys did the reporting that Steve Ballmer could be such a booster for college sports that he would get run around by Uncle Dennis on, hey, let's not pretend that any of these rules in sports are real. Let's not pretend that any of these rich people that salary cap actually happens to matter to Steve Ballmer who will just go through sports like, hey, I'll just kick this golf ball, right? I don't have to play golf real.

quotes.speaker: Jessica Smetana
quotes.summary_phrase: Lack of connection between PolyMarket and the Philadelphia 76ers
quotes.excerpt: There's no connection between PolyMarket and the 76ers. So to me, that's the part that if it was something like Fanatics.
quotes.quote: There's no connection between PolyMarket and the 76ers. So to me, that's the part that if it was something like Fanatics, if he was doing a deal with Fanatics book for 15 million and was rolling it out that way, then there's a more obvious connection or a more head-scratching decision. But on top of that, it doesn't really make sense to me where these betting companies keep using these big names in sports. It does not. Sydney Sweeney will not drive people to that app. LeBron will not drive people to that app. These margins in betting are so much smaller than people realize and you're seeing that as other betting companies start laying people off, stop doing ambassador deals. And they still think that Tom Brady or LeBron James or Kevin Hart is going to move the needle for them and it simply does not.

quotes.speaker: Jeremy Taché
quotes.summary_phrase: Rich Paul's influence on the prediction market during the offseason
quotes.excerpt: Rich Paul was out there all offseason, seemingly influencing the prediction market.
quotes.quote: The thing that becomes the question with this one in particular is that Rich Paul was out there all offseason, seemingly influencing the prediction market. We saw him out there swaying which way people thought LeBron was going to go over the course of the time. It was just Tyrese Maxey's name circle. The question that I've seen a lot of people asking online is more surrounding that element of it, which is him influencing that market before LeBron gets this deal.

quotes.speaker: Amin Elhassan
quotes.summary_phrase: Philadelphia's active pursuit of LeBron James in the offseason
quotes.excerpt: I feel like Philly was as in the race as anyone was, as anyone in basketball.
quotes.quote: I feel like Philly was as in the race as anyone was, as anyone in basketball. And so if you look at, for example, Bob Myers going on Rich Paul's podcast and literally giving the pitch of like, hey, if you come to Philly, this is what we would do and why we would love to have you and all that. I feel like every team, but why were the numbers for Philly always so low? Because I think people were not drawn by the narrative, right? Where the narrative for Cleveland was like, come home, ended it at home, right? And the narrative for Golden State, play with your best friend Stephen Curry, and the narrative here is like, make good with Pat Riley who left the key under the mat and all that.
